prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 8.6. Exact Sanskrit: यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।
तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥ ६ ॥ Exact stored meaning: O Kaunteya, whatever state of being one remembers when one finally leaves the body — that state alone is reached, always having been absorbed in that very state of being. Chapter context: The imperishable, remembrance, transition, cosmic cycles and paths. Use symbolic contemplative imagery without depicting bodily distress, corpses or literal metaphysical claims as historical events. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: And whoever, at the time of death, departs remembering Me alone, leaving the body — that person attains My state (mad-bhāvaṃ). Of this there is no doubt. Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight. With mind and intellect surrendered to Me (mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ), you shall come to Me alone — without doubt. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

entry.alt: Interpretive watercolor for Bhagavad Gītā 8.6: O Kaunteya, whatever state of being one remembers when one finally leaves the body — that state alone is reached, always having been absorbed in that very state of being.
